content:
kevin: Ran a set of mixed streaming + non-streaming replay runs on the staging cluster. Observed readloop 'hysteresis' where chunking flips between small continuous chunks (streaming) and large batched outputs, causing throughput oscillation and sporadic latency spikes. Perf-bot posted a short summary below.

perf-bot: SUMMARY: 6 runs, 3 workloads (pure-stream, pure-nonstream, mixed). Mixed-run variance high: 95th latency 2.6x non-stream baseline. CPU scheduling bubbles correlated with frequent kernel switches (int8 -> fused attention) and KV cache miss bursts. See /tmp/perf/1836720456/attach.log :eyes:

ria: Can you paste the harness commands + the exact replay config you used? want to reproduce locally quickly. :thumbsup:

kevin: Sure. Command I used (staging, 8xA10g):

```
./replay_harness --mode mixed --clients 120 --trace replay/2026-03-mix.json \
  --target qps 150 --max-rt 1200 --chunking chunky --client-readloop adaptive --kv-cache=on
```

Replay config differences: mixed trace alternates 60% streaming requests (avg chunk 160 tokens) and 40% non-stream (single full response ~900 tokens). Important: client-readloop=adaptive enabled hysteresis timer=25ms (default).

anna: Noted. The KV cache pattern matters — when streaming requests interleave with long non-stream ones, we get a lot of cache eviction/rehydration. That bumps kernel selection because the runtime tries to swap to a kernel variant optimized for long sequences. If the batch suddenly shrinks again, we flip kernels and recompile hot paths.

sam: Did you capture kernel selection traces? want to know how often we switch per-second and CPU stall time.

kevin: Yup, pulled perf trace + kernel log. Relevant excerpt:

```
KERNEL_SWITCH_LOG:
  00:00:12.102 - select kernel int8_fused_attn (seq=128, batch=32)
  00:00:12.108 - select kernel fp16_block_attn (seq=768, batch=8)  <-- switch due to long seq
  00:00:12.146 - switch back to int8_fused_attn (seq=160, batch=28)
  00:00:12.307 - select kernel fp16_block_attn (seq=860, batch=6)
\nSAMPLE_STATS:
  avg_batch_size: mixed=18.4, stream=26.7, nonstream=7.2
  kv_cache_hitrate: mixed=0.71, stream=0.85, nonstream=0.22
  sched_cpu_bubble_ms: mixed=74ms avg, nonstream=24ms avg
```

kevin: TL;DR: kernel switch churn and KV misses align with those latency spikes. Looks like the adaptive readloop tries to minimize latency by shrinking the batch too aggressively when it sees a long request, but that then causes the runtime to pick a different kernel, which is expensive.

anna: Proposed mitigation: add a small "batching hysteresis" window so the readloop waits up to 40ms before committing to drop to tiny batches, and treat kernel selection as a soft signal — avoid immediate kernel swap until stable for N requests. Also bump KV cache pin threshold for sequences >512 to avoid immediate eviction.

ria: Sounds reasonable. How did apples-to-apples look? i.e., pure-stream vs mixed where we artificially keep kernel fixed (force-kernel).

kevin: Good call. I ran controlled runs with `--force-kernel=int8_fused_attn` and `--force-kernel=fp16_block_attn`. Results: forcing int8_fused_attn on mixed workload improved 95th latency by ~28% vs adaptive but decreased median throughput for very long sequences (expected). Forcing fp16 for entire run raised cost per-token ~1.6x but smoothed latency spikes. So tradeoff exists.

sam: Do we have an easy perf/regression test to catch this? would like a small CI job that runs a short mixed replay and asserts 95p latency delta vs baseline < 1.5x.

kevin: I sketched one: `tests/perf/mixed_hysteresis_smoke` — 90s replay, injects long/non-long pattern, collects kernel_switch_count, kv_miss_rate, 95p latency. Pass criteria: kernel_switch_count < 10/s and kv_miss_rate_diff < 0.15 vs baseline. I'll push the harness and a baseline artifact to the perf-bucket.

ana: small nit: can we also log the client readloop decisions (why it shrank batch this window) into trace so we can correlate? adds very low overhead.

kevin: yep will add a compact event: `readloop.hysteresis_event` with reason tags (time-window, long-seq-detected, kv-miss).

perf-bot: ARTIFACTS UPLOADED: gs://redwood-perf/1836720456/ (kernel_logs.tar.gz, replay_summary.json, baseline-ints.tgz)

ria: ok let's iterate: PR to change readloop hysteresis to 40ms + pin threshold bump, add smoke CI job. if CI green we'll run 5x longer staging runs and decide if we backport to stable. @kevin can you open PR and assign anna + sam? :rocket:

kevin: will do in ~30m. thanks all.

sam: :+1:
